faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about the 2026 edition.

items.q: When will the 2026 edition be published?
items.a:
The 2026 edition of Algeria Banking Index is expected to be published in September 2026.

Subscribers will be notified as soon as the study is available.

items.q: What will be the scope of the 2026 edition?
items.a: The 2026 edition will cover 21 banks operating in Algeria. It will focus primarily on comparing 2024–2025 performance, complemented by an analysis of trends observed over the 2023–2025 period.

The study will offer a consolidated analysis of the Algerian banking sector, comparisons between public and private banks, individual analyses of 21 institutions, as well as rankings and benchmarks by indicator.

This edition will also be enriched with new insights on off-balance sheet items, workforce, banking network, and operational performance.

It will also include a section dedicated to banking user experience — mobile app, web e-banking, and branch services — through the ABIX 2026 Barometer.

items.q: What does the early subscription guarantee?
items.a:
Early subscription allows you to reserve the 2026 edition before its publication and benefit from a 10% preferential rate.

Upon publication, deliverables corresponding to the subscribed pack will be made available to the subscriber.

Yes. Any subscription registered by August 31, 2026 at 23:59 (Algerian time) benefits from the early subscription rate.

This rate remains guaranteed until the study is delivered.

items.q: What are the different offer levels?
Can I receive a pro forma invoice?
items.a: Yes. Upon request, Tadjeddine & Partners can issue a pro forma invoice for the selected pack to facilitate your organization's internal procurement procedure.

items.q: Can I subscribe for multiple users?
items.a:
Yes.

The Essential Pack is designed for 1 user.

The Pro Pack allows access for up to 3 users belonging to the same entity.

The Corporate Executive Pack allows access for up to 20 users belonging to the same entity.

items.q: Are the 2024 data identical to those in the previous edition?
items.a:
Not necessarily.

Some banks have performed reclassifications or restatements of certain financial line items in subsequent publications.

To ensure maximum consistency with 2025 data, the 2026 edition uses the most recent revised 2024 data available.

These numbers replace those used in the previous edition where necessary.

items.q: Will the Banking Services Barometer influence financial results or bank rankings?
items.a:
No.

The Banking Services Barometer is a distinct section dedicated to user experience and satisfaction regarding banking services — mobile app, web e-banking, and branch services.

Its results do not alter the financial data of institutions.

They will be presented separately, along with a description of the methodology used and representativeness information.

items.q: Will the study feature perspectives from bank executives and experts?
items.a:
The 2026 edition also plans to host signed contributions from bank executives and experts, subject to editorial confirmation.

These contributions will be clearly distinguished from Algeria Banking Index's independent analysis.

They will not enter into indicator calculations, rankings, or independent conclusions.

items.q: Is the 2025 edition included in the 2026 subscription?
items.a:
No.

The 2025 edition remains an independent publication and can be acquired separately.

For organizations wishing to obtain both 2025 and 2026 editions, a bundled proposal can be arranged upon request.

items.q: What happens if the publication date changes?
items.a:
Subscribers will be notified of any changes to the publication timeline.

The subscription will remain valid and the preferential rate secured before August 31, 2026 will remain guaranteed.

items.q: Can I request a presentation or a custom benchmark?
items.a:
Yes.

The Corporate Executive Pack includes a briefing session and a custom benchmark.

Additional advisory services, such as a presentation to a board of directors or an in-depth analysis, can also be offered separately.

hero.title: Study Methodology
hero.subtitle: A structured approach to collect, consolidate, compare, and interpret financial, operational, and public data relating to the Algerian banking sector.
hero.introText: Algeria Banking Index studies rely on the methodical use of publicly available information, its harmonisation, and comparative analysis. The objective is to provide a consistent reading of performance, trends, and positioning across covered institutions.

disclaimerBox.title: What the methodology does NOT constitute
disclaimerBox.p1: The published analyses do not constitute a credit rating, a prudential rating, a solvency certification, a financial audit, or an investment recommendation.
disclaimerBox.p2: They rely on publicly available information and a comparative methodology proprietary to Algeria Banking Index studies.

approach.title: Our 6-Step Analytical Approach
approach.description: Algeria Banking Index studies rest on structured collection of publicly available information, followed by consolidation, consistency verification, comparison, and interpretation.

steps.title: Scope & Data Collection
steps.body: Identification and extraction of information published by banks and available institutional sources: financial statements, annual reports, and other relevant financial or operational disclosures.

steps.title: Consolidation, Consistency & Restatements
steps.body: Data consistency verification, reconciliation of aggregates, and standardized treatment of information across institutions and fiscal years.
steps.note: When banks subsequently publish restated or reclassified historical data, studies adopt the latest available revised data to preserve comparative consistency.

steps.title: Definition & Standardization of Indicators
steps.body: Standardized definition of indicators used, distinguishing between stock data, flow data, and financial ratios.
steps.note: Calculations cover growth, profitability, efficiency, market shares, and indicators enabling the comparison of institutional trajectories.

steps.title: Sector Comparisons & Positioning
steps.body: Analysis of sector aggregates, public vs. private bank comparisons, evolution of market shares, and relative positioning of institutions across studied indicators.
steps.badge: Methodological Principle: Comparisons are conducted on an identical methodological basis across all covered institutions.

steps.title: Individual Analyses & Operational Dimensions
steps.body: Each institution undergoes an individual review of its evolution, positioning, and core performance indicators.
steps.note: Subject to data availability and comparability, analysis may also integrate operational metrics such as off-balance sheet commitments, workforce, branch network, and operational productivity.

steps.title: Review, Analysis & Interpretation
steps.body: Consolidated data is analyzed and interpreted by Mr. Rachid Sekak and Tadjeddine & Partners to identify meaningful shifts, industry trends, and factors explaining observed trajectories.
steps.note: Factual findings, calculations, and interpretations are distinguished wherever possible in the study deliverables.

revisions.title: Historical Data and Revisions
revisions.p1: Historical data may evolve over time.
revisions.p2: Some banks may perform reclassifications or restatements for previous financial years in subsequent publications.
revisions.p3: When a revised figure is published by an institution, Algeria Banking Index may substitute this figure for the one used in an earlier edition to maintain consistent comparative series.
revisions.p4: Numbers in a new edition may therefore occasionally differ from those in a previous edition without implying an error.

ebanking.title: Specific Methodology for the Banking Services Barometer
ebanking.p1: The Banking Services Barometer constitutes a complementary and independent pillar alongside financial analysis.
ebanking.p2: It is based on a survey of banking service users to measure satisfaction levels and perceptions of offered services.
ebanking.p3: Barometer results are presented separately from financial indicators. They do not enter into financial ratio calculations or accounting-based rankings.
ebanking.p4: Published results specify respondent sample size, data collection period, response distribution, and representativeness parameters.

contributions.title: Editorial Contributions
contributions.p1: Certain editions may feature signed contributions from bank executives or industry experts.
contributions.p2: These contributions are clearly identified and separate from analysis produced by Algeria Banking Index.
contributions.p3: They reflect the authors' opinions and do not enter into calculations, comparisons, or independent study conclusions.

sources.title: Sources and Limitations
sources.p1: Analyses are prepared from public information available at the closing date of each edition.
sources.p2: Data availability, detail level, and presentation format may vary across institutions.
sources.p3: When data is unavailable or cannot be homogenously compared, it may be excluded from specific indicators or flagged explicitly.

methodology.disclaimerText: This analysis focuses exclusively on information identified on the official websites of the institutions during the review conducted by ABIX. The absence of an identified document on a website does not necessarily mean that it has not been produced, submitted to competent authorities, or distributed through other channels. The score measures the online availability and timeliness of accessible information. It constitutes neither an assessment of the intrinsic quality of accounts, nor an evaluation of regulatory compliance, governance, or financial strength.

items.short_definition: Measures the overall financial size of a bank by aggregating all its assets and uses of funds.
items.detailed_definition: Total Assets represents the sum of all asset items on the balance sheet as of December 31 (cash, securities, customer loans, fixed assets). In ABIX, it serves as the primary metric for measuring bank size and market share.
items.formula: Total Actifs = Caisse & Banques centrales + Titres & Bons du Trésor + Crédits clientèle + Autres actifs
items.interpretation: A high balance sheet indicates market scale and intermediation capacity within the banking system.
items.example: The aggregate balance sheet of the 21 banks reaches around 22,000 billion DZD, with nearly 88% held by public banks.

items.short_definition: Total funds entrusted to the bank by households, corporates, and institutions as demand, term, or savings deposits.
items.detailed_definition: As the primary liability resource, customer deposits measure deposit collection capacity and customer trust. In ABIX, multi-year deposit growth is compared against loans to assess liquidity dynamics.
items.formula: Dépôts Totaux = Dépôts à vue + Dépôts à terme + Comptes d'épargne + Autres dépôts clientèle
items.interpretation: Steady deposit growth strengthens bank funding stability without excessive reliance on money markets.
items.example: In 2022-2023, customer deposits grew by +6.2% exceeding 14,600 billion DZD.

items.short_definition: Total gross amount of financings, overdrafts, and credit facilities extended to households, businesses, and public entities.
items.detailed_definition: Customer loans represent the core earning asset of a universal bank. ABIX monitors lending growth, transformation ratios, and relative financing to the real economy.
items.formula: Crédits Bruts = Crédits d'exploitation + Crédits d'investissement + Crédits immobiliers + Crédits aux particuliers
items.interpretation: Reflects direct financing of economic activity and generates the majority of interest revenues.
items.example: Total loan stock to the economy reached approx. 8,840 billion DZD in 2023, with an overall transformation ratio of ~60%.

items.short_definition: Equivalent to a bank's net operating revenue, calculated as net interest margin plus net fee income and trading gains.
items.detailed_definition: Net Banking Income measures the gross revenue generated across all banking and intermediation operations. It serves as the denominator for the Cost-to-Income ratio and operational efficiency metrics.
items.formula: PNB = (Produits d'intérêts - Charges d'intérêts) + (Commissions perçues - Commissions payées) + Gains/pertes de change et titres
items.interpretation: Consistent NBI growth highlights commercial vitality and balanced asset/service pricing.
items.example: BEA generated 112.4 billion DZD of NBI, ranking 2nd nationally behind BNA.

items.short_definition: Difference between NBI and operating expenses (personnel costs, admin overhead, depreciation).
items.detailed_definition: GOI measures pure operational profitability prior to any loan impairment charges (cost of risk) or tax expenses.
items.formula: RBE = Produit Net Bancaire - Frais de personnel - Autres charges générales d'exploitation - Dotations aux amortissements
items.interpretation: A growing positive GOI shows revenues comfortably absorb infrastructure, branch, and staff operating expenses.
items.example: For an NBI of 100M DZD and 40M DZD operating expenses, GOI stands at 60M DZD.

items.short_definition: Final profit or loss remaining after deducting all expenses, loan loss provisions, and corporate income taxes.
items.detailed_definition: The bottom-line figure of the income statement, Net Profit serves to pay dividends to shareholders and strengthen regulatory equity capital via retained earnings.
items.formula: Résultat Net = RBE - Dotations nettes aux provisions pour créances + Produits/charges exceptionnels - Impôts sur les bénéfices (IBS)
items.interpretation: Measures overall profit generation and forms the numerator for Return on Equity (ROE) and Return on Assets (ROA).
items.example: Aggregate banking sector net income increased by +14.8% reaching 225.6 billion DZD in 2023.

items.short_definition: Permanent capital belonging to shareholders, including share capital, retained earnings, reserves, and current profit.
items.detailed_definition: Shareholders' Equity acts as the primary solvency buffer absorbing potential loan losses. In ABIX, it is evaluated through the Equity-to-Assets ratio and leverage capacity.
items.formula: Fonds Propres = Capital Social + Primes d'émission + Réserves légales et statutaires + Report à nouveau + Résultat de l'exercice
items.interpretation: High equity cushions ensure resilience against macroeconomic shocks and enable financing larger syndications.
items.example: The median Equity-to-Assets ratio across Algerian banks stands around 8.3%.

items.short_definition: Sovereign debt securities issued by the Algerian State and held as assets by commercial banks.
items.detailed_definition: Treasury bills constitute a major asset holding for Algerian banks, especially state-owned banks. They provide secure interest yields with zero regulatory risk-weighting.
items.formula: BDT = Bons du Trésor à court terme (BTCT) + Bons du Trésor assimilables (OAT)
items.interpretation: High sovereign bond holdings boost liquidity and regulatory ratios but may yield lower returns than private corporate lending.
items.example: State-owned banks hold the vast majority of the sovereign bond portfolio in the domestic market.

items.short_definition: Financial commitments given or received by the bank not immediately recorded on the balance sheet (guarantees, letters of credit).
items.detailed_definition: Off-balance sheet operations capture foreign trade financing and public procurement support (bid bonds, performance bonds), generating fee income without upfront cash outlay.
items.formula: Engagements Hors-Bilan = Cautions et avals donnés + Engagements de financement accordés + Crédits documentaires ouverts
items.interpretation: High off-balance sheet volume signals strong positioning in trade finance and major infrastructure projects.
items.example: BEA and BNA record massive off-balance sheet exposures due to their central role in oil and industrial import-export transactions.

items.short_definition: Measures a bank's ability to generate net income per unit of equity capital invested by shareholders.
items.detailed_definition: ROE is the benchmark metric for financial profitability. In ABIX, it is computed on closing equity as well as average equity (ROAE) to smooth capital variations during the financial year.
items.formula: ROE = (Résultat Net / Fonds Propres Comptables) × 100
items.interpretation: An ROE exceeding 12-14% is considered strong performance in the Algerian banking environment.
items.example: With an ROE of 14.8%, BEA and Al Baraka (16.4%) rank in the top quartile (Q4) for equity returns.

items.short_definition: Smoothed variation of ROE calculating net income relative to the average equity between start and end of the period.
items.detailed_definition: ROAE provides a more accurate metric than simple ROE when a bank undergoes capital increases or major dividend payouts during the year.
items.formula: ROAE = Résultat Net / ((Fonds Propres t + Fonds Propres t-1) / 2) × 100
items.interpretation: Delivers an unbiased measure of equity efficiency throughout the entire financial period.
items.example: With 15 billion DZD net income and equity rising from 100 to 110 billion: ROAE = 15 / 105 = 14.29%.

items.short_definition: Measures how effectively a bank converts its total asset base into net profit.
items.detailed_definition: ROA measures macroeconomic asset efficiency independently of leverage or capitalization structure. In banking, a ROA of 1 to 2% represents high asset productivity.
items.formula: ROA = (Résultat Net / Total Actifs) × 100
items.interpretation: A high ROA indicates the bank optimizes earnings per balance-sheet unit without relying on unsafe leverage.
items.example: Private banks often post higher ROA (1.8% to 2.3%) than large public lenders (1.2% to 1.6%) driven by wider loan spreads.

items.short_definition: Smoothed version of ROA calculating net income over average total assets across the financial year.
items.detailed_definition: ROAA neutralizes intra-year balance sheet expansion to accurately capture average asset productivity.
items.formula: ROAA = Résultat Net / ((Total Actifs t + Total Actifs t-1) / 2) × 100
items.interpretation: Preferred indicator by international credit analysts to benchmark banks undergoing rapid asset expansion.
items.example: Algerian banking median ROAA stands at approximately 1.52%.

items.short_definition: Percentage of Net Banking Income consumed by operating expenses and depreciation.
items.detailed_definition: The Cost-to-Income ratio is the central benchmark of bank operational efficiency. A lower percentage reflects leaner operations and superior cost discipline.
items.formula: Coefficient d'Exploitation = (Frais Généraux d'Exploitation + Amortissements) / Produit Net Bancaire × 100
items.interpretation: Under 45% signifies superior efficiency; 45% to 60% indicates standard cost control; above 65% signals heavy overhead eating into margins.
items.example: BEA records a Cost-to-Income ratio of 34.2% (Top Q1), while the market average is 42.6%.

items.short_definition: Ratio comparing net interest earnings on loans and bonds against total interest-bearing assets.
items.detailed_definition: NIM measures the core unit profitability of traditional lending and deposit intermediation activities.
items.formula: Marge Nette d'Intérêt = (Produits d'intérêts - Charges d'intérêts) / Actifs Productifs Moyens × 100
items.interpretation: A high NIM indicates pricing power on loans or a strong base of zero-cost demand deposits.
items.example: Average sector NIM stands around 3.40% in the Algerian market.

items.short_definition: Average Net Banking Income generated per full-time bank employee over the year.
items.detailed_definition: This indicator measures the return on human capital and the degree of branch/back-office automation.
items.formula: Productivité = Produit Net Bancaire / Effectif Total de la Banque (ETP)
items.interpretation: Private and corporate banks frequently exceed 20-30M DZD/employee due to streamlined headcount and corporate focus.
items.example: BEA posts 18.2M DZD NBI/employee (92nd sector percentile) against a market average of 14.8M DZD.

items.short_definition: Ratio comparing regulatory capital against the bank's total risk-weighted assets (RWA).
items.detailed_definition: Core international Basel prudential standard implemented by the Bank of Algeria, requiring minimum total regulatory capital above 9.5% - 12% of risk-weighted assets.
items.formula: Ratio de Solvabilité = (Fonds Propres Réglementaires / Actifs Pondérés des Risques - RWA) × 100
items.interpretation: A ratio above 15-18% reflects a solid safety buffer supporting credit expansion without capital constraints.
items.example: The average capital adequacy ratio across Algerian banks stands at 17.8%, well above regulatory floors.

items.short_definition: Net impairment charges set aside by the bank to cover potential loan defaults relative to total average loan portfolio.
items.detailed_definition: The cost of risk gauges the underlying quality of the credit book and provisioning prudence against non-performing loans.
items.formula: Coût du Risque = (Dotations nettes aux provisions pour créances / Encours moyen de crédits bruts) × 100
items.formula_latex: \text{Coût du Risque} = \frac{\text{Dotations Nettes aux Provisions}}{\text{Encours Moyen de Crédits}} \times 100
items.interpretation: A low cost of risk (< 0.5%) reflects clean credit quality. A spike signals rising borrower distress.
items.example: BEA posts a controlled cost of risk of 0.65%, whereas specialized agricultural lenders reach 1.45%.

items.short_definition: Share of loans with delayed repayments or high default probability relative to total gross loans.
items.detailed_definition: The NPL ratio is the standard measure of bank asset quality, encompassing substandard, doubtful, and loss classifications under Bank of Algeria rules.
items.formula: Taux NPL = (Créances Non Performantes / Total des Crédits Bruts) × 100
items.formula_latex: \text{Ratio NPL} = \frac{\text{Créances Douteuses et Litigieuses}}{\text{Total Crédits Bruts}} \times 100
items.interpretation: A lower NPL ratio indicates disciplined underwriting and active debt recovery.
items.example: The sector NPL ratio is closely tracked to assess macroeconomic cycle impacts on corporate borrowers.

items.short_definition: Percentage of non-performing loans already covered by accumulated loss provisions on the balance sheet.
items.detailed_definition: This ratio measures balance sheet protection against realized loan defaults: fully provisioned bad debts prevent surprise income hits upon write-off.
items.formula: Taux de Couverture = (Provisions Cumulées pour Dépréciation de Crédits / Total Créances Non Performantes) × 100
items.interpretation: A coverage ratio above 75-80% reflects prudent balance sheet management and strong loss absorption capacity.
items.example: The average provision coverage ratio across the Algerian banking market stands at 84.2%.

items.short_definition: Proportion of total assets financed directly by equity without borrowing or customer deposits.
items.detailed_definition: Unweighted leverage metric. Unlike risk-weighted CAR, it provides a straightforward, unmodeled view of true capital strength.
items.formula: Ratio FP / Bilan = (Fonds Propres Comptables / Total Bilan) × 100
items.interpretation: A higher ratio shields depositors and significantly curtails insolvency risk.
items.example: Median Equity-to-Assets ratio across the Algerian banking sector: 8.32%.

items.short_definition: Number of times a bank's total assets exceed its equity capital base.
items.detailed_definition: Financial leverage multiplies asset return (ROA) into equity return (ROE). High leverage amplifies gains during good years but heightens insolvency risk under asset deterioration.
items.formula: Levier = Total Bilan / Fonds Propres = 1 / (Ratio Fonds Propres / Bilan)
items.interpretation: A multiple of 10x to 12x is standard for prudent commercial banking institutions.
items.example: For a balance sheet of 1,000B DZD and 100B DZD equity, the leverage multiple is 10.0x.

items.short_definition: Statistical metric measuring how many standard deviations of return decline a bank can withstand before exhausting equity.
items.detailed_definition: The Bank Z-Score combines return on assets (ROA), capitalization (Equity/Assets), and historical return volatility. A higher score reflects greater distance to insolvency.
items.formula: Z-Score = (ROA moyen + (Fonds Propres / Total Actifs)) / Écart-type(ROA)
items.interpretation: A high Z-score signifies superior earnings stability and stout equity protection against volatility.
items.example: Utilized in ABIX advanced benchmarks to evaluate bank stability across macroeconomic cycles.

items.short_definition: International supervisory framework evaluating banks across 6 pillars: Capital adequacy, Asset quality, Management, Earnings, Liquidity, Sensitivity to market risk.
items.detailed_definition: The CAMELS model serves as the benchmark framework for central bank supervisors and credit rating agencies assessing financial institutions.
items.formula: Évaluation multicritère des 6 dimensions (Capital, Asset quality, Management, Earnings, Liquidity, Sensitivity)
items.interpretation: Provides a holistic 360° health check without overemphasizing pure asset volume.
items.example: ABIX incorporates the core principles of CAMELS into its 360° Bank Profile and Four Dimensions framework.

items.short_definition: Percentage of total customer deposits redeployed into customer loans.
items.detailed_definition: LDR measures bank transformation intensity and liquidity cushioning. Below 70-80% reflects excess liquidity, while over 100% indicates the bank relies on external wholesale funding.
items.formula: LDR = (Total Crédits Bruts Clientèle / Total Dépôts Clientèle) × 100
items.interpretation: In Algeria, the average LDR is moderate (~60.4%), highlighting structural sector liquidity and substantial lending headroom.
items.example: Al Baraka posts an LDR of 94.1% (active participatory banking model) compared to 58.2% for BNA.

items.short_definition: Measures the mean annualized growth rate of a financial metric over a multi-year period, smoothing out year-to-year swings.
items.detailed_definition: CAGR computes the constant annualized rate required for a metric to grow from its initial value to its ending balance over n periods. In ABIX, 3-year and 5-year CAGRs are tracked across balance sheet and P&L aggregates.
items.formula: CAGR = ((Valeur Finale / Valeur Initiale)^(1 / n)) - 1
items.interpretation: A CAGR of 8% means the aggregate expanded at an annualized average rate of 8% throughout the analyzed timeframe.
items.example: Total Assets expanding from 100B DZD in 2020 to 125.97B DZD in 2023 (3 years): CAGR = (125.97 / 100)^(1/3) - 1 = +8.0% per annum.

items.short_definition: Percentage change in a financial metric compared directly against the previous year's figure.
items.detailed_definition: Measures short-term annual trajectory across financial aggregates from one financial close to the next.
items.formula: YoY = ((Valeur t - Valeur t-1) / Valeur t-1) × 100
items.interpretation: Helps identify rapid market accelerations or operational slowdowns between consecutive financial periods.
items.example: Total banking assets: +8.4% YoY in 2023.

items.short_definition: Value dividing an ordered distribution of banks into two equal halves: 50% fall below and 50% above.
items.detailed_definition: In the Algerian banking sector where large state lenders dominate total volume, the median provides a far more representative market benchmark than the arithmetic mean, avoiding distortion from extreme outliers.
items.formula: Valeur au rang central (N+1)/2 d'une série ordonnée de N banques
items.interpretation: Represents the true central baseline of the domestic banking market.
items.example: The median banking ROE stands at 11.8% (differing from the asset-weighted aggregate mean).

items.short_definition: Values that split the ordered population of banks into four equal groups, each containing 25% of observations.
items.detailed_definition: Q1 marks the 25th percentile (lower 25% cutoff), Q2 marks the median (50%), and Q3 represents the 75th percentile (top 25% threshold). Q4 denotes top-quartile performers.
items.formula: Q1 = 25e percentile, Q2 = 50e percentile (médiane), Q3 = 75e percentile
items.interpretation: Ranking in quartile Q1 for Cost-to-Income means being among the top 25% most efficient institutions (since lower is better).
items.example: BEA ranks in the Top 15% (Q4) on ROE and in Q1 (efficient) on Cost-to-Income.

items.short_definition: Indicates the exact percentage of banks in the sector that score below a specific bank's value.
items.detailed_definition: Percentiles position any bank along a normalized 0-to-100 scale across the 21 peer institutions, regardless of the underlying metric scale.
items.formula: Percentile = (Nombre de banques avec valeur inférieure / Nombre total de banques) × 100
items.interpretation: An 88th percentile ranking signifies the bank outperforms 88% of its peer group on that metric.
items.example: On NBI/employee productivity, BEA ranks at the 92nd market percentile.

items.short_definition: Measures the dispersion of individual bank values around the sector average.
items.detailed_definition: A larger standard deviation indicates wide performance disparities across institutions. In ABIX, it determines confidence bands and outlier detection thresholds.
items.formula: Écart-type = Racine carrée de la moyenne des écarts au carré par rapport à la moyenne
items.interpretation: In a normal distribution, ~68% of banks fall within ±1.0σ of the mean, and ~95% within ±2.0σ.
items.example: Used to calibrate anomaly thresholds on cost of risk or LDR ratios.

items.short_definition: An observation deviating with statistical significance from sector-wide distribution baselines.
items.detailed_definition: ABIX identifies outliers deterministically using Z-Scores (> ±2.0σ warning, > ±3.0σ critical) and Interquartile Range (IQR). Outliers often indicate unique business models (e.g., Islamic finance) or one-off shocks.
items.formula: |Z| = |(X - Moyenne) / Écart-type| > 2.0 ou X hors de [Q1 - 1.5×IQR, Q3 + 1.5×IQR]
items.interpretation: An outlier is not inherently negative: it flags a distinct positioning requiring dedicated qualitative review.
items.example: Al Baraka emerges as an LDR outlier (+3.1σ, 94.1% vs median 64.1%) due to its Islamic financing structure.

items.short_definition: Measures the number of standard deviations a specific value sits above or below the population mean.
items.detailed_definition: Z-Scores allow cross-comparison of financial variables with different units (e.g. DZD, percentages, headcount) onto a unified zero-centered scale.
items.formula: Z = (Valeur observée - Moyenne) / Écart-type
items.interpretation: A Z of 0 equals the mean; Z of +2.0 places the institution in the upper 2.5% tail.
items.example: AGB scores a Z-Score of +2.6σ on NBI growth, highlighting notable outperformance.

items.short_definition: Mathematical transformation mapping any financial indicator onto a uniform 0 (lowest) to 100 (best) scale.
items.detailed_definition: Used in 360° radar charts and multidimensional matrices to combine disparate criteria into balanced comparable scores.
items.formula: Score = ((Valeur - Valeur Min) / (Valeur Max - Valeur Min)) × 100
items.interpretation: Enables immediate intuitive visual assessment of strengths and improvement areas on radar plots.
items.example: A score of 100 is assigned to the top-performing bank, and 0 to the lowest.

items.short_definition: Indexing technique setting a baseline year to 100 to compare relative growth trajectories across banks of differing sizes.
items.detailed_definition: Base 100 indexing plots relative growth speeds of massive state lenders and agile private banks on the same normalized chart.
items.formula: Indice Année t = (Valeur Année t / Valeur Année de Base) × 100
items.interpretation: An index of 135 in 2024 (base 100 in 2020) represents +35% cumulative growth over the period.
items.example: Applied in ABIX Historical and Comparator modules to analyze multi-year growth trajectories.

items.short_definition: Measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two financial variables.
items.detailed_definition: The coefficient ranges from -1 (perfect inverse correlation) to +1 (perfect positive correlation), with 0 indicating no linear relationship.
items.formula: r = Covariance(X, Y) / (Écart-type(X) × Écart-type(Y))
items.interpretation: Helps empirically verify whether larger bank balance sheets translate into superior profitability margins.
items.example: Correlation between Total Assets and ROE is moderate, confirming asset scale alone does not guarantee superior returns.

items.short_definition: Percentage of the total banking industry aggregate represented by an individual bank (Assets, Deposits, Loans, or NBI).
items.detailed_definition: Market share reflects a bank's scale and competitive footprint. ABIX computes market shares across Assets, Deposits, Loans, and NBI, tracking yearly gains and losses.
items.formula: Part de Marché = (Agrégat de la Banque / Total Agrégat des 21 Banques) × 100
items.interpretation: The 6 state-owned banks hold approx. 88% aggregate asset market share, versus 12% across all private institutions.
items.example: BNA (26.8%) and BEA (21.9%) together represent nearly half of the entire Algerian banking market.

items.short_definition: Difference in percentage points between a bank's market share in the current year versus the previous year.
items.detailed_definition: Identifies which institutions gain or lose market traction in deposits, lending, or assets, independent of overall market expansion.
items.formula: Variation PDM = Part de Marché t - Part de Marché t-1 (en points de %)
items.interpretation: A gain of +0.82 percentage points denotes growth outpacing the broader market average.
items.example: BEA gained +0.82 points of total asset market share in 2022, the strongest gain in the sector.

items.short_definition: Subset of banks sharing homogeneous characteristics (size, public/private ownership, business model) for meaningful benchmarking.
items.detailed_definition: Comparing a mid-sized private lender directly against public mega-banks can skew insights. ABIX isolates relevant peer cohorts (Public banks, International private banks, Islamic banks) for objective relative evaluation.
items.formula: Segmentation par critères : Statut (Public/Privé), Taille (Top 5 / Intermédiaires), Modèle (Universel / Islamique)
items.interpretation: Evaluates whether a bank outperforms direct competitors operating under identical regulatory and market conditions.
items.example: Al Baraka is benchmarked against its specific peer cohort of Islamic and private banks.

items.short_definition: Algorithmic grouping of banks displaying similar multidimensional financial profiles (profitability, leverage, efficiency, growth).
items.detailed_definition: ABIX identifies distinct structural clusters in Algeria: 1) Large universal public institutions, 2) High-profitability private lenders, 3) Growth-oriented expansion banks, 4) Niche/Islamic institutions.
items.formula: Classification par analyse en composantes principales (ACP) et K-Means sur les ratios clés
items.interpretation: Highlights the rich diversity of operating models across the Algerian banking landscape.
items.example: Visualized on the ABIX Growth vs Profitability Strategic Matrix.

items.short_definition: Total set of licensed commercial banks with published certified financial statements included in the study.
items.detailed_definition: ABIX covers the entirety of commercial banks operating in Algeria: 20 banks in the 2025 edition (2023-2024 data) and 21 banks in the 2026 edition (including Ziraat Bankasi).
items.formula: Périmètre = 6 Banques Publiques + 15 Banques Privées / Mixtes = 21 Banques
items.interpretation: Ensures comprehensive representative coverage of the Algerian market without sampling bias.
items.example: 21 banks analyzed covering 100% of commercial banking assets in Algeria.

items.short_definition: Multi-year analysis method retaining the identical bank cohort across years to avoid distortion from market entries or exits.
items.detailed_definition: Guarantees measured sector growth is organic rather than an artifact of adding a new bank into the dataset.
items.formula: Agrégat Constant = Somme des grandeurs des banques présentes à la fois en Année t et en Année t-1
items.interpretation: Ensures scientific rigor in ABIX multi-year trend comparisons.
items.example: Applied when computing sector-wide growth rates over 2022–2025.

items.short_definition: Structural comparison of performances, balance sheets, and operating models across state-owned versus private banks.
items.detailed_definition: Algeria features a dual banking landscape: 6 state lenders hold ~88% of assets through dense branch networks, while 15 private banks deliver higher unit profitability (ROE, ROA) on selective customer segments.
items.formula: Agrégat Public = Σ Banques Publiques | Agrégat Privé = Σ Banques Privées
items.interpretation: Highlights complementarity between public balance sheet scale and private operational agility.
items.example: Private banks maintain an equity return edge (ROE 14.6% vs 11.4% public) despite running fewer branches.

items.short_definition: Global benchmark metric measuring market concentration by summing the squared market shares of all competing banks.
items.detailed_definition: HHI ranges from 0 to 10,000 points. International standards classify: 1) < 1,500 = Unconcentrated, 2) 1,500 - 2,500 = Moderately Concentrated, 3) > 2,500 = Highly Concentrated.
items.formula: HHI = Somme des (Part de marché de chaque banque en %)^2
items.interpretation: With an asset HHI around 1,742 points, the Algerian banking sector falls into the moderately concentrated tier, shaped around a sturdy public core.
items.example: BNA (26.8% -> 718 pts) + BEA (21.9% -> 480 pts) + CPA (15.2% -> 231 pts) contribute over 80% of the aggregate HHI.

items.short_definition: Theoretical number of equal-sized banks that would generate the exact same HHI concentration as the current market.
items.detailed_definition: Translates abstract HHI points into an intuitive count: while 21 licensed banks operate, market share skew means the market economically behaves like ~5.7 equal-sized banks.
items.formula: Nombre Effectif = 10 000 / HHI
items.interpretation: The closer to 21, the more balanced the market. A figure of 5.7 captures the scale asymmetry between mega-lenders and boutique private banks.
items.example: For an HHI of 1,742, the effective number of banks equals 10,000 / 1,742 = 5.74 equivalent banks.

items.short_definition: Cumulative market share held by the top 3 banking institutions (BNA + BEA + CPA).
items.detailed_definition: Measures top-tier oligopoly concentration. A CR3 above 60% indicates a tight oligopoly where the top 3 leaders anchor systemic liquidity and pricing.
items.formula: CR3 = Part de Marché Rang 1 + Part de Marché Rang 2 + Part de Marché Rang 3
items.interpretation: In Algeria, CR3 reaches 63.9% of total assets, highlighting the dominant footprint of the top 3 state banks.
items.example: BNA (26.8%) + BEA (21.9%) + CPA (15.2%) = 63.9% of total assets.

items.short_definition: Cumulative market share held by the top 5 banking institutions (BNA, BEA, CPA, BADR, CNEP).
items.detailed_definition: CR5 gauges the combined market dominance of the primary Tier-1 banking group in financing the national economy.
items.formula: CR5 = Somme des parts de marché des 5 premières banques
items.interpretation: CR5 reaches 82.0% of total assets in Algeria, showing that Tier-1 state banks concentrate the vast bulk of banking resources.
items.example: The top 5 banks assemble over 18,000B DZD out of the 22,000B DZD total industry assets.

items.short_definition: Transparent benchmarking framework avoiding arbitrary global scores, structured around 4 distinct pillars: 1. Profitability, 2. Growth, 3. Efficiency, 4. Capitalization.
items.detailed_definition: ABIX avoids opaque single-score rankings. The 4D framework delivers an objective multidimensional read where institutions are benchmarked on verifiable metrics.
items.formula: Piliers : 1. Rentabilité (ROE, ROA, NIM) | 2. Croissance (CAGR Actifs, Dépôts, PNB) | 3. Efficacité (CIR, PNB/Agent) | 4. Capitalisation (FP/Actifs, Solvabilité)
items.interpretation: Allows executive leadership and analysts to quickly grasp an institution's distinct profile without methodology shortcuts.
items.example: A bank may excel in profitability while remaining in consolidation mode regarding growth.

items.short_definition: Visual positioning cross-referencing NBI growth rate (X-axis) and ROE equity profitability (Y-axis) against sector medians.
items.detailed_definition: The matrix segments banks into 4 quadrants: 1) Dynamic Leaders (High growth, High ROE), 2) Resilient Profitability (Moderate growth, High ROE), 3) Investment & Expansion (High growth, Moderate ROE), 4) In Transformation (Moderate growth, Moderate ROE).
items.formula: Axes centrés sur la Médiane Secteur : Axe X = Croissance PNB % | Axe Y = Rentabilité ROE % | Taille bulle = Total Bilan
items.interpretation: Provides an instant snapshot of commercial momentum and financial return across every banking player.
items.example: BEA and Al Baraka position inside the Dynamic Leaders quadrant.

items.short_definition: Objective score evaluating the accessibility and timeliness of audited financial statements and annual reports on official bank websites.
items.detailed_definition: Structured on 2 dimensions (Financial Statements publication /3 pts and Annual Activity Report /3 pts) for a total global score of 6 points.
items.formula: Score Global (0 à 6) = Score Publication des Comptes (0 à 3) + Score Rapport d'Activité (0 à 3)
items.interpretation: Measures adherence to best practices in public financial disclosure and investor relations.
items.example: 3 banks achieve the perfect score of 6/6 (CPA, BDL, ABC), while the market average sits at 2.7/6.

items.short_definition: Algorithmic engine automatically scanning all 21 balance sheets to detect trend breaks, structural divergences, and executive signals.
items.detailed_definition: Unlike black-box AI generative models, ABIX strategic alerts are 100% deterministic, auditable, and directly traceable to certified published financial line items.
items.formula: Règles déterministes : Divergence Dépôts/Crédits, Rupture de Marge, Écart de Provisionnement (> ±2σ), Érosion PNB vs Résultat
items.interpretation: Supplies executive committees and boards with an instant, verified briefing on key structural market developments.
items.example: Detected alert: sector deposits (+6.2%) expanded faster than loans (+5.1%), widening the aggregate liquidity cushion.

items.short_definition: Periodic market survey assessing customer adoption, digital usage, and user satisfaction across web, mobile banking, and branch networks.
items.detailed_definition: Operational complement to balance sheet data, the Barometer links certified financial performance with real-world digital customer adoption in Algeria.
items.formula: Enquête quantitative et qualitative : Canaux digitaux, Ergonomie, Disponibilité, Tarification, Sécurité
items.interpretation: Sheds light on customer digital expectations and technological readiness across Algerian institutions.
items.example: 2026 Edition: in-depth comparative benchmark of mobile banking app features in Algeria.
